correctness.rationale: For n≥3 both graphs have diameter two, so the forbidden triples consist of a nonadjacent pair with a common neighbor. In the modified graph the only ≥3-vertex faces using a nonedge are the two triangles on p1,p2,q1 and p1,p2,q2. The clique part is the join of the path p1–q2–q1–p2 with n−2 zero-spheres. Each triangle collapses along its matched-pair edge, which has no other proper coface. The remaining complex is the contractible join with n−1 extra edges attached at their endpoints. Quotienting this contractible CW subcomplex gives the claimed bouquet by a homotopy equivalence. The intact complex is the cross-polytope boundary with n endpoint-attached intervals; since the boundary is path connected, these attachments give n circle summands. The identity on vertices does not give an inclusion either way: {p1,p2,p3} is lost and {p1,p2,q1} is gained. This proves the integral claims, including n=3. An independent Floyd–Warshall/exhaustive-triple check at n=3,4 reproduced the face descriptions and mod-two ranks; it is corroboration only.

value.rationale: This is a natural perturbation of a canonical graph family and an explicit witness of non-monotone metric-complex behavior. It exhibits an unbounded dimension in which a single edge change eliminates integral homology while also changing the free fundamental group. The actual wedge equivalence and the lack of a common inclusion convey more than a polynomial or small-instance Betti calculation.
